name: Hexagon Playground module notation
//: `module X` / `end module X` are the Playground's own way of declaring a second
virtual file, not `.hex` syntax: a real Hexagon module IS a file (spec/modules.md
§2), so the VS Code grammar deliberately has no counterpart and must not grow one.
This is an injection rather than an edit to syntaxes/hexagon.tmLanguage.json for
exactly that reason — the shared grammar stays the language, and the one construct
only Playground understands is added on top, where only Playground loads it.
`L:` puts these patterns ahead of the injected-into grammar's own, which is what
they need: `module` and `end` are ordinary NonUpperNames to the base grammar and
would otherwise be claimed as terms first.
The selector deliberately carries no `-comment -string` exclusion. src/workspace-
source.ts scans raw lines and knows nothing of strings or comments, so a line
inside a multi-line string that reads exactly `module X` really does open a
virtual file. Painting it as one shows the user that surprise rather than hiding
it; excluding those contexts would make the editor disagree with the host.

patterns.//: The opening header. Anchored to a whole line, as src/workspace-source.ts requires: the notation is recognized only when it is the entire line.
The closing header. `end module` is scoped as one keyword run because that is what it is — neither word means anything without the other.
